items.title: Susan Doyle, CEO, and Erin Goodyear, Director of Emergency and Congregate Services, Services and Housing in the Province (SHIP)
notes:
Susan Doyle and Erin Goodyear provided an overview of SHIP's services and highlighted SHIP's accomplishments in providing supportive housing and wraparound services to communities across Ontario. 

In response to the Committee, E. Goodyear indicated that Council can best support SHIP by continuing existing collaboration and having ongoing funding discussions.

E. Goodyear emphasized the importance of working with community partners to provide effective wraparound services that focus on the specific needs of each individual in need of support. She also noted that SHIP has established Community Advisory Committees within each of the communities where SHIP programs exist, meeting monthly to discuss any concerns.

In response to the Committee, S. Doyle confirmed that SHIP receives funding from all levels of government.

E. Goodyear confirmed that SHIP's transitional programs are tailored to the specific needs of each individual. She clarified that there is no time limit to how long an individual can stay in SHIP's emergency housing program, but that the transitional housing program is two years with the opportunity for a one-year extension, and the supportive housing program is a five-year program with the opportunity for a two-year extension. She also noted that all program participants have access to all available wraparound supports.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PDL-BWR-26-004, CYPT and UNICEF Canada – Youth Impact Survey Partnership
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, provided an introduction to the report, noting that findings from the Youth Impact Survey are intended to inform evidence-based, cross-sector action and ensure that youth perspectives are meaningfully reflected in policies, programs, and service delivery.

Alison Pearson, Manger, Children and Youth Planning Table, highlighted that the Youth Impact Survey has now launched for the fourth time in Waterloo Region. 

Lydia MacKay Swiatkowska, of UNICEF Canada, outlined the UNICEF index of child and youth well-being and noted that this framework has informed the development of the Youth Impact Survey. She highlighted several examples of how the Youth Impact Survey has resulted in tangible benefits, including funding to support child and youth well-being and strategic plans aligned to the needs and desires of young people.

Inspector Aaron Mathias, of Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS), highlighted that WRPS used the previous Youth Impact Survey to inform the development of its current Youth Engagement Strategy and that the survey allows systems to be responsive to community need.

In response to the Committee, A. Pearson clarified that the Children and Youth Planning Table (CYPT) has over 100 member organizations and 72 of these organizations have opted to become voting member organizations, meaning that these 72 organizations have taken an intentional step to tie their organization's work to the CYPT's collaborative work. She also indicated that the 72 voting member organizations are constantly evolving but currently include the cities of Cambridge, Kitchener, and Waterloo as well as the townships of Wilmot and Woolwich. 

A. Pearson confirmed that there has been a trend towards further involvement with the CYPT from the Region's area municipalities. She also confirmed that the Youth Impact Survey captures nine domains of well-being through generalized survey questions, but that there is an opportunity for respondents to provide additional, more specific feedback through an open-ended question at the end of the survey.

A. Pearson clarified that the survey will be open for the full month of May and will take place every three years. She also noted that the sample size target is 2,000 survey respondents.

A. Pearson confirmed that all youth living within Waterloo Region aged 9-18 are invited to participate in the survey.

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-CUL-26-011, Doon Heritage Village Re-Opening Update
notes:
Julian Kingston, Director, Cultural Services, provided an overview of updates that have been made to Doon Heritage Village after its temporary closure in 2023 to undertake infrastructure improvements and community engagement. He noted the upcoming re-opening date of July 1, 2026.

J. Kingston noted that upgrades included utilities modernization, WIFI capability, accessibility improvements, and conservation treatments for artifacts. He also highlighted Doon Village's new tagline, "One Village, Many Stories," which reflects its focus on expanded storytelling and perspectives as part of a new brand identity.

In response to questions from the Committee regarding revenue, J. Kingston confirmed that school programs, rentals, and public admissions will provide revenue streams for Doon Village upon its re-opening.

Stacy McLennan, Acting Manager, Region of Waterloo Museums and Archives, highlighted that accessibility upgrades to Doon Village included new ramps, re-orienting of ramps, upgrades to gravel pathways to improve wheelchair accessibility, and the addition of an on-site adult change table.

J. Kingston clarified that through the Museum Community Membership Program, non-profit organizations can obtain group memberships for their members.

In response to the Committee, J. Kingston noted that Doon Village will be expanding its storytelling to include additional eras outside of 1914, as well as collaborating with partner organizations to expand storytelling to include the history of Indigenous and Black communities in the Region.

Wayne Steffler, Chief Financial Officer, confirmed that Doon Village has an annual net operating cost of approximately $700,000.

In response to the Committee, staff confirmed that they will bring back additional information to the next Council meeting on the possibility of free admission to Doon Village on Canada Day.

J. Kingston confirmed that Doon Village retained an active base of volunteers during its closure period.

J. Kingston also confirmed that summer camp programming will resume at Doon Village this summer, and that the Museum gift shop features merchandise that relates to Doon Village. 

Received for information.

items.title: PHP-PSV-26-003, 2025 Community Paramedicine Program Report
notes:
Ann Bettles, Commander, Paramedic Services, provided an overview of the key principles of the Community Paramedicine Program, including the provision of safe, proactive, and accessible care outside of the traditional 911 response system to connect patients with the right care at the right time.

A. Bettles highlighted program accomplishments from 2025, including the expansion of the program from five to nine full time community paramedics and 7,500 interventions for 400 clients in the last six months of the year. She also noted that the program receives 100% of its funding from the Province.

A. Bettles outlined the planned 2026 expansions for the program, including expansion of clinic locations, launch of mobile clinic services, and continued collaboration with community partners. 

A. Bettles also shared the official Community Paramedicine Program logo.

In response to the Committee, A. Bettles confirmed that partnerships exist between the Community Paramedicine Program and community organizations to provide services on site at these organizations. She also noted that it is the hope that the modelled good work of the program will assist in securing future funding.

A. Bettles confirmed that the Community Paramedicine Program is available in all areas of the Region. She also clarified that the program typically receives client referrals through primary care providers, hospitals, or from frontline 911 paramedics, noting that if clients are not eligible to be referred to the program, they receive assistance to connect with other resources. 

A. Bettles confirmed that staff can explore advocacy options and suggestions for Council to bring to the 2026 AMO Conference.

In response to the Committee, A. Bettles emphasized that the program's focus is to ensure that people are connected with the most appropriate service for their healthcare needs and that healthcare services complement one another, rather than overlap.

Received for information.

N. Salonen joined the meeting at 10:11 a.m.
